This intermediate on treatment with $\text{Br}_2$/Red P followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ yields 2-bromobutanoic acid as the major product. Identify the starting alkyl halide 'X'.
questions.question: An unknown alkyl halide 'X' undergoes substitution with KCN, followed by acidic hydrolysis to form an intermediate. This intermediate on treatment with $\text{Br}_2$/Red P followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ yields 2-bromobutanoic acid as the major product. Identify the starting alkyl halide 'X'.
questions.solution:
The final product is 2-bromobutanoic acid, which is formed via the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.

Working backwards, the intermediate carboxylic acid before the HVZ reaction must be butanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$).

Butanoic acid is formed by the acidic hydrolysis of butanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$).

Since the reaction of an alkyl halide with KCN involves a step-up of one carbon atom, the starting alkyl halide 'X' must contain 3 carbon atoms in a straight chain.

Therefore, 'X' is 1-chloropropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$).

Reaction sequence:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(i) } \text{Br}_2\text{/Red P}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{COOH}$

Answer: 1-Chloropropane

Consider the following reactions of 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane:
(i) 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{aq. KOH, }\Delta}$ A (major)
(ii) 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, }\Delta}$ B (major)

Identify the major products A and B.
questions.question:
Consider the following reactions of 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane:
(i) 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{aq. KOH, }\Delta}$ A (major)
(ii) 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, }\Delta}$ B (major)

Identify the major products A and B.
questions.solution:
The nature of the solvent plays a crucial role in determining whether an alkyl halide undergoes substitution or elimination with KOH.

In reaction (i), aqueous KOH is used. In an aqueous medium, the hydroxide ion ($\text{OH}^-$) acts primarily as a nucleophile, leading to nucleophilic substitution. The bromine atom in 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane is replaced by a hydroxyl group, yielding 2-methylcyclopentanol as the major product A.

In reaction (ii), alcoholic KOH is used. In an alcoholic medium, the alkoxide ions formed act as strong bases, favouring dehydrohalogenation ($\beta$-elimination). The $\beta$-hydrogens are located on C2 (which bears the methyl group) and C5.

According to Zaitsev's rule, elimination occurs predominantly to give the most substituted alkene. Removing the proton from C2 yields 1-methylcyclopentene (a trisubstituted alkene), while removing it from C5 yields 3-methylcyclopentene (a disubstituted alkene). Thus, 1-methylcyclopentene is the major product B.

Option 2 is incorrect because it swaps the functions of aqueous and alcoholic KOH.
Option 3 is incorrect because it identifies the less substituted Hofmann product for the elimination reaction.
Option 4 is incorrect because it assumes a carbocation rearrangement occurs during the substitution step to form a tertiary alcohol.

Answer: A = 2-methylcyclopentanol, B = 1-methylcyclopentene

Since $\text{AgNO}_2$ is predominantly covalent, the nucleophilic attack occurs through the nitrogen atom, yielding nitroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NO}_2$) as the major product A. In the second step, nitroethane (A) is reduced by $\text{Sn/HCl}$ to form a primary amine, ethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$), which is product B.

In the final step, ethanamine (B) reacts with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and ethanolic $\text{KOH}$. This is the carbylamine reaction, which is specific to primary amines, producing a foul-smelling isocyanide. Thus, product C is ethyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$).

Therefore, A is Nitroethane and C is Ethyl isocyanide.

Answer: $\text{A} = \text{Nitroethane}$; $\text{C} = \text{Ethyl isocyanide}$

questions.question:
Consider the following four alkyl bromides:
(A) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br}$
(B) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(C) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\mathrm{CHCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(D) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{CCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$

Predict the correct decreasing order of their reactivity towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction.
questions.solution:
In an $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction, the nucleophile attacks the $\alpha$-carbon from the side opposite to the leaving group. The rate of reaction is inversely proportional to the steric hindrance around the $\alpha$-carbon.

All the given compounds are methyl or primary bromides. However, as the branching at the $\beta$-carbon increases, steric crowding in the transition state increases, which significantly lowers the rate of the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction.

(A) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br}$ has no alkyl groups and is the least hindered.
(B) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ has one methyl group at the $\beta$-carbon.
(C) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\mathrm{CHCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ (isobutyl bromide) has two methyl groups at the $\beta$-carbon.
(D) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{CCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ (neopentyl bromide) has three methyl groups at the $\beta$-carbon and is the most hindered.

Thus, the steric hindrance increases in the order: (A) < (B) < (C) < (D).
Consequently, the decreasing order of reactivity towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ is: (A) > (B) > (C) > (D).

Answer: (A) > (B) > (C) > (D)

When the $\alpha$-halo acid A is treated with alcoholic KOH and heated, it undergoes $\beta$-elimination (dehydrohalogenation). The halogen atom is removed from the $\alpha$-carbon and a hydrogen atom is removed from the adjacent $\beta$-carbon.

This elimination yields an unsaturated carboxylic acid, propenoic acid (also known as acrylic acid), as the major product B.

Using aqueous KOH instead of alcoholic KOH would have resulted in nucleophilic substitution to form 2-hydroxypropanoic acid.

Answer: Propenoic acid
